extracted_stakeholders.name: REDD+ Program
extracted_stakeholders.role: An international framework for protecting forests and achieving sustainable development goals by acting on environmental governance and environmental justice.

extracted_stakeholders.name: Indonesian Government
extracted_stakeholders.role: Responsible for implementing REDD+ strategies and policies at the national level.

extracted_stakeholders.name: Indigenous Groups
extracted_stakeholders.role: Local communities that rely on forests for their livelihoods and are affected by deforestation and REDD+ initiatives.

extracted_stakeholders.name: European Commission
extracted_stakeholders.role: Influences policy and provides environmental targets related to forest conservation.

extracted_stakeholders.name: Global Forest Watch
extracted_stakeholders.role: Provides monitoring and assessment of forest areas, contributing to the evaluation of REDD+ effectiveness.

extracted_stakeholders.name: Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)
extracted_stakeholders.role: Publishes reports and data relevant to forest management and deforestation rates.

extracted_stakeholders.name: Indonesian REDD+ Task Force
extracted_stakeholders.role: Develops and executes strategies to manage and implement REDD+ in Indonesia.

extracted_factors.Label: Deforestation in Indonesia
extracted_factors.Description: Deforestation is a major contributor to Indonesia's greenhouse gas emissions and a central issue targeted by climate policies, including REDD+.

extracted_factors.Label: REDD+ Implementation Challenges
extracted_factors.Description: Challenges in effectively implementing REDD+, including stakeholder management and monitoring and evaluation of the initiatives.

extracted_factors.Label: International Development Cooperation
extracted_factors.Description: External support necessary for countries like Indonesia to undertake conservation efforts due to lack of local incentives.

extracted_factors.Label: Indigenous Population Vulnerability
extracted_factors.Description: Indigenous and vulnerable populations face challenges in the political process, affecting their ability to benefit from REDD+ initiatives.

extracted_pain_points.description: There are complexities in engaging with multiple stakeholders with varying interests, particularly indigenous groups that are affected by deforestation.
Economic activities such as oil palm cultivation and timber plantation contribute significantly to deforestation, competing with conservation efforts.
Weak institutional frameworks and poor governance hinder the full realization of REDD+ goals in Indonesia.
Insufficient funding hinders Indonesia's ability to meet its climate change mitigation targets despite its significant commitments.
Challenges in establishing effective monitoring, reporting, and verification systems affect the transparency and accountability of REDD+.
